title: Reconstruction Semantics Consolidation Review
purpose: Review MPF-RSEM-001 through MPF-RSEM-009 as a coherent semantic reconstruction scaffold and determine whether semantic exploration remains safe for continued theorem-oriented local analysis.
review_findings: Semantic persistence metrics successfully quantify interpretive stability without truth claims.
Deformation modes effectively track meaning degradation under sequentialization and flattening.
Participatory interpretation is rigorously constrained to embedded observer limits.
Translation corridors provide stable cross-domain mapping while preserving domain-specific tensions.
Recursive reference behavior is successfully bounded to prevent closure absolutism.
Semantic conflict preservation is enforced as a mandatory structural indicator.
Drift detection provides a linguistic firewall against semantic inflation and ontology promotion.
Stress tests confirm robustness against injected absolutism and closure claims.
remaining_risks: Persistence scores may be psychologically misread as degrees of truth in informal contexts.
Recursive feedback complexity requires continuous participatory-interpretation monitoring.
Semantic translation granularities remain qualitative and dependent on audit completeness.
